steps.title: Reader extracts medicines, visits and warnings
Program checks every quote and number against the document
Checker compares the plan with the document
Explainer writes it in plain English
Scheduler builds the timetable and calendar (plain Python)
Program checks every number the Explainer wrote

extraction.diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia (lung infection) of the right lower lobe. Type 2 diabetes with high blood sugar (hemoglobin A1c 10.4%).
extraction.hospital_summary: You were treated with IV antibiotics and your breathing improved. Your blood sugar was high, so we started a long-acting insulin.

medications.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate (Augmentin)
special_instructions: Finish all of it even if you feel better.
medications.source_quote:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate (Augmentin) 875 mg-125 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food for 5
days. Last dose: evening of 10/21/2026. Finish all of it even if you feel better.

medications.name: Insulin glargine (Lantus SoloStar)
medications.purpose: lowers blood sugar overnight and through the day.
medications.source_quote:
Insulin glargine (Lantus SoloStar) 100 units/mL pen. Inject 18 units under the skin once daily at bedtime.
Purpose: lowers blood sugar overnight and through the day.

medications.name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol)
medications.max_per_day: Do not take more than 3,000 mg in 24 hours.
medications.source_quote:
Acetaminophen (Tylenol) 500 mg tablet. Take 2 tablets (1,000 mg) by mouth every 8 hours as needed for fever
or pain. Do not take more than 3,000 mg in 24 hours.

medications.name: Benzonatate
medications.source_quote:
Benzonatate 100 mg capsule. Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily as needed for cough. Swallow whole;
do not chew.

medications.name: Metformin
special_instructions:
This was paused in the
hospital; restart it at home.
medications.source_quote:
Metformin 1,000 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with breakfast and dinner. This was paused in the
hospital; restart it at home.

appointments.source_quote:
Primary care, Dr. Laura Chen: Friday 10/23/2026 at 9:15 AM, Maplewood Primary Care, Suite 110. Bring your blood
sugar log.

appointments.purpose: to make sure the pneumonia has cleared
appointments.source_quote:
Chest X-ray: in 6 weeks to make sure the pneumonia has cleared. The order is placed; Radiology will call you to
schedule.
Diabetes educator: call (203) 555-0119 to schedule an insulin teaching visit this week.

signs: you still have a fever above 101 F after 3 days of antibiotics

your blood
sugar is above 300 two times in a row
watery diarrhea more than 3 times a day
warnings.source_quote:
Call Dr. Chen's office at (203) 555-0110 if: you still have a fever above 101 F after 3 days of antibiotics; your blood
sugar is above 300 two times in a row; you get a rash, or watery diarrhea more than 3 times a day.

warnings.who_to_call: 911 or go to the emergency room
signs: your lips or face turn blue or gray

you
become confused or very sleepy
your blood sugar is below 54 and does not come up after treatment
warnings.source_quote:
Call 911 or go to the emergency room if: you have trouble breathing; your lips or face turn blue or gray; you
become confused or very sleepy; your blood sugar is below 54 and does not come up after treatment, or you pass
out.

instructions.text:
Blood glucose meter and test strips. Check your blood sugar before breakfast and before dinner every day and
write the numbers down.
instructions.source_quote:
Blood glucose meter and test strips. Check your blood sugar before breakfast and before dinner every day and
write the numbers down.

instructions.text: Rest, and slowly increase your activity.
instructions.source_quote: Rest, and slowly increase your activity.

instructions.text: Drink plenty of water unless another doctor has told you to limit fluids.
instructions.source_quote: Drink plenty of water unless another doctor has told you to limit fluids.

instructions.text:
Low blood sugar: if your sugar is below 70, eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar (4 ounces of juice or 4 glucose
tablets), wait 15 minutes, and check again.
instructions.source_quote:
Low blood sugar: if your sugar is below 70, eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar (4 ounces of juice or 4 glucose
tablets), wait 15 minutes, and check again.

explanation.summary: You were in the hospital because you had a lung infection called pneumonia in the lower part of your right lung. You also have type 2 diabetes, and your blood sugar was very high. You were treated with antibiotics through an IV, your breathing got better, and you were started on a long-acting insulin to help control your blood sugar.

m1.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth 2 times a day, with food, for 5 days. Take it at 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM. Your last dose is the evening of 10/21/2026.
tips: Your last dose will be the evening of 10/21/2026.
Finish all of this medicine, even if you start to feel better.

m2.what_for: It lowers your blood sugar overnight and through the day.
m2.how_to_take: Inject 18 units under your skin 1 time a day, at 9:00 PM.

m3.how_to_take: Take 2 tablets (1,000 mg) by mouth every 8 hours if you need it, for fever or pain. Do not take more than 3,000 mg in 24 hours.

m4.how_to_take: Take 1 capsule by mouth up to 3 times a day if you need it, for cough.

m5.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth 2 times a day, with breakfast and dinner. Take it at 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.
tips: This medicine was stopped while you were in the hospital. Start taking it again now that you are home.

signs: You still have a fever above 101°F after 3 days of taking the antibiotic.
Your blood sugar is above 300 two times in a row.
You have watery diarrhea more than 3 times in one day.

w2.who_to_call: 911 or go to the emergency room
signs: Your lips or face turn blue or gray.
You become confused or very sleepy.
Your blood sugar is below 54 and does not come back up after treatment.

i1.text: Check your blood sugar before breakfast and before dinner every day, using your blood sugar meter and test strips. Write down the numbers each time.

i2.text: Rest, and slowly do a little more activity each day as you feel able.

i3.text: Drink plenty of water, unless another doctor has told you to limit how much you drink.

i4.text: If your blood sugar is below 70, eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar, like 4 ounces of juice or 4 glucose tablets. Wait 15 minutes, then check your blood sugar again.

a1.text: See your primary care doctor, Dr. Laura Chen, on 2026-10-23 at 9:15 AM at Maplewood Primary Care, Suite 110. Bring your blood sugar log with you.

a2.text: You will need a chest X-ray in 6 weeks to make sure the pneumonia has cleared up. The office will call you to set up the appointment.

a3.text: Call the diabetes educator this week at (203) 555-0119 to set up a visit where they teach you about your insulin.

labels.summary: Why you were in the hospital
labels.emergency: Call 911 or go to the emergency room
labels.times_note: Clock times are suggestions. Your papers say how often (for example, twice daily); Going Home spreads the doses across the day. Keep the spacing and move them to fit your day, or ask your pharmacist.
labels.first_day_note: On the day you leave the hospital, ask the nurse which of today's doses were already given, so none are doubled.
